feature: y_lag0, y_lag1, y_lag2, y_lag3 (log cases this week and 1-3 weeks back)
mechanism: Dengue spreads from person to mosquito to person, so this week's cases seed the next transmission cycles; reporting delays also make recent counts the best measure of the current epidemic level
notes: shi2016: recent incidence at lags 1-5 weeks generally improved forecasts. colongonzalez2021 and buczak2014 both use lagged cases as inputs. SHAP gives this group 48-76% of the attention (research/results/STATUS.md).

feature: y_mean4, y_mean12 (4- and 12-week average of log cases)
mechanism: Smooths week-to-week reporting noise, giving the epidemic level and how long it has been building
notes: Rolling averages are a smoothed version of the lags above; same evidence.

feature: y_trend (change in log cases over 3 weeks)
mechanism: Growth rate: a rising curve signals transmission is accelerating ahead of the peak
notes: No source tests a trend feature directly; shi2016 supports short case lags in general. Mechanism is standard epidemic growth.

feature: y_lastyear (log cases in the same week last year)
mechanism: Captures the area's usual seasonal level; also carries immunity after a large year (a big year is often followed by a smaller one)
expected_direction: positive (usual level); can be negative after a large epidemic year
notes: colongonzalez2021's baseline is a seasonal average and the full model beat it only 1-3 months ahead, so last year's level carries much of the signal. vanpanhuis2015: 2-5 year multiannual cycles mean last year can mislead after an epidemic year (see Provinces 2020 vs 2019 in causes.md).

feature: rain_lag0 ... rain_lag11 (weekly rain, this week to 11 weeks back)
mechanism: Rain fills containers that become Aedes breeding sites; eggs to adults take about 1-2 weeks, then the virus needs incubation in the mosquito and the person, so cases follow rain by several weeks
expected_direction: positive up to a point; very heavy rain can flush breeding sites
notes: sumi2017: dengue related to rain over the prior 6-7 weeks; seasonal rain cycle leads dengue by about 2 months. carvajal2018: rain cross-correlation peaks at lag 5 weeks. iguchi2018: non-linear, highest risk at 32 mm (RR 1.67), max lag tested 12 weeks. tuan2024 lagged climate 2-20 weeks. Person A found rain's SHAP share peaks at the longest lag offered (10-11 weeks); literature lags go to 12-20 weeks, so a longer window is worth testing.

mechanism: Cumulative wetness keeps containers full long enough for several mosquito generations
notes: Same evidence as the rain lags; totals match sumi2017's 'rain over the prior 6-7 weeks'.

feature: heavy_days8 (heavy-rain days in the last 8 weeks)
mechanism: Heavy rain can create breeding sites but also flush larvae from containers; extreme wetness lowered risk in a regional study
expected_direction: mixed (positive at moderate levels; negative at extremes)
notes: ith2025: extremely wet conditions reduced risk (RR 0.89) across 291 Southeast Asian locations. iguchi2018: risk peaks at a moderate weekly rain (32 mm), not the highest.

feature: rh_lag0, rh_lag2, rh_lag4, rh_lag6, rh_lag8 (mean relative humidity)
mechanism: Humid air lets adult mosquitoes live longer and feed more often, so more of them survive the virus's incubation period
notes: carvajal2018: humidity was the top weather factor in the best model, lag 4 weeks. xu2020: relative humidity was the only factor linked to the second seasonal peak (threshold 77%). shi2016: absolute humidity over the last month predicted cases 4-5 weeks ahead; high humidity 15-20 weeks before was negative. sumi2017: humidity cycle leads dengue by about 1 month.

feature: temp_lag0, temp_lag2, temp_lag4, temp_lag6, temp_lag8 (mean temperature)
mechanism: Warmth speeds mosquito development, biting and viral incubation; above about 29-30 C mosquito survival falls, so the effect is an inverted U
expected_direction: positive up to about 27.5-29 C then negative
notes: seposo2023 (61 PH provinces): risk rises from 15.8 C to a peak at 27.5 C, then falls; lag up to 18 weeks. mordecai2017: transmission peaks at 26-29 C. iguchi2018 (Davao): higher RR at 26 C, lower at 27-31 C. carvajal2018: mean temperature cross-correlation at lag 17 weeks. sumi2017: temperature cycle leads dengue by about 4 months. Because the effect is non-linear, trees (LightGBM) suit it better than a linear term.

feature: tmax_max4 (highest daily maximum temperature in the last 4 weeks)
mechanism: Very hot days shorten mosquito life and can suppress transmission
notes: mordecai2017: Ae. aegypti transmission drops to zero above 34.6 C. carvajal2018: maximum temperature cross-correlation at lag 18 weeks. Philippine lowland maxima rarely pass 34 C, so the effect may be small.

mechanism: Captures the yearly rainy-season cycle and school and holiday patterns that drive the annual epidemic
notes: olana2025: national peaks July-September. sumi2017: one-year cycle explains dengue and weather. xu2020: peaks in August (south) and September (NCR).

mechanism: More people means more reported cases at the same rate; acts as the area's scale
notes: mordecai2017 and shi2016 use log population as a covariate, not as a tested driver. Fixed per area, so in a pooled model it also works as an area label (research/results/METHODS.md).

feature: heat_band4, heat_band4_lag4 (days with mean temperature 26-29 C in the last 4 weeks, and 4 weeks earlier)
mechanism: Counts days in the band where mosquitoes transmit most efficiently
notes: mordecai2017: peak transmission 26-29 C. seposo2023: Philippine risk peaks at 27.5 C. The band itself is from mordecai2017; a day count is Person A's design.

feature: heat_hot4 (days at or above 34 C maximum in the last 4 weeks)
mechanism: Days hot enough to cut mosquito survival
notes: mordecai2017: transmission upper limit 34.6 C. ith2025: heatwaves (above the local 95th percentile) raised risk after 2 months up to 7 days a month (RR 1.28), so effects of heat extremes are not simply negative. Mixed mechanism, little direct evidence.

mechanism: Combines temperature and humidity, the two factors that set mosquito survival
notes: No verified study of the heat index and dengue. Its parts (temperature, humidity) have strong evidence, so it may duplicate them.

mechanism: Cool nights slow mosquito development and viral incubation
notes: carvajal2018: minimum temperature cross-correlation at lag 13 weeks. Person A notes the cached province weather lacks daily minimum (METHODS.md).

mechanism: A wide daily swing lowers transmission near the optimum temperature
notes: liuhelmersson2014 (mechanistic): near 29 C a small range raises epidemic potential and a large one lowers it. tuan2024: temperature range lagged 14 weeks was among the selected features (seen only in a page summary). Not built yet: needs daily minimum.

mechanism: Same as the province temperature features, now for the live regional model
notes: Same evidence as the province temperature rows.

mechanism: Same as the province humidity features, now for the live regional model
notes: Same evidence as the province humidity row. xu2020 is at region level, which matches this panel.

feature: enso_oni, enso_oni_lag3 (Oceanic Nino Index, about 2 and 5 months back)
mechanism: El Nino brings warmer, drier conditions to the Philippines, changing temperature, water storage and rain months ahead; it lines up multi-year dengue cycles across Southeast Asia
expected_direction: positive in El Nino years (warmer); timing varies
notes: vanpanhuis2015: 2-5 year dengue cycles across 273 provinces were highly coherent with the ONI. carvajal2018: SOI cross-correlation at lag 20 weeks. buczak2014 used SOI and sea surface temperature anomaly as inputs. The evidence is for multi-year cycles: 5 years of province data hold about one cycle, so a forecasting model may learn ENSO as a year label (Person A's hypothesis 1).

mechanism: Higher ground is cooler, slowing mosquitoes and the virus; also less urban
notes: sy2026 (nationwide PH): elevation linked to force of infection but NOT to reported incidence, which varied unpredictably. edillo2022: altitude had no significant main effect on Philippine Ae. aegypti egg traits. buczak2014 included altitude among inputs. Fixed per area, so in a forecast that already knows each area's recent cases it may add little.

mechanism: Low-lying land is warmer and more urban, with more standing water
notes: sy2026: urban low-elevation barangays had the highest force of infection (13.2%). edillo2022 defines lowland as below 100 m. Same caveat as mean elevation: linked to infection, not to reported cases.

mechanism: Crowding raises the chance an infected mosquito bites a new person
notes: sy2026: density linked to force of infection but not reported incidence. seposo2023: denser provinces showed higher dengue risk at the upper temperature range (an interaction, not a main effect).

feature: heatwave days (days above the local 95th percentile for 2+ days)
mechanism: Short heat spells speed transmission; long ones cut mosquito survival
expected_direction: positive up to about 7 days a month then negative
notes: ith2025: fewer than 12 heatwave days a month raised risk after a 2-month lag, highest at 7 days (RR 1.28). Uses a local threshold, unlike the fixed 34 C in heat_hot4.

mechanism: In drought people store water in containers that become breeding sites
notes: ith2025: drought (scPDSI -4) raised risk (RR 1.85), and extreme wetness lowered it. One study only; needs a monthly drought index per area.

mechanism: Long lags capture several mosquito generations and the build-up before the season
notes: tuan2024 lagged climate 2-20 weeks; seposo2023 used up to 18 weeks; shi2016 allowed 1-20 weeks. Person A's SHAP shows rain's share peaks at the longest lag offered (10-11 weeks).

mechanism: Dengue spreads between nearby areas through travel
notes: buczak2014 used adjacent-province incidence as an input. vanpanhuis2015 found travelling waves between provinces. Not tested on its own in either.
